quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What is the most important thing in any driving situation?
questions.explanation: Every driving situation has three basic parts: the environment, the vehicle, and the driver. Only you as a driver can see what is happening. Use your skills, knowledge, and judgment to make safe decisions.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If a yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection, you should continue through carefully.

questions.question: What are highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions called?
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about potential dangers. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them could cause an accident.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask oncoming drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accident scenes just to look.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the train has passed.
Yes, when the lights have stopped flashing.

questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train horns. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to sleet or snow?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Allow more distance between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance because slippery roads need more space to stop.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Do not turn on any vehicle lights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only when the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles allowed to use?

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are allowed to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: Which one must you obey above all the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before all signs, signals, and road markings. This includes police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: How do you get most of the information needed to drive safely?
questions.explanation: Almost all information needed to drive safely comes from what you see. Always be aware of what is happening around your vehicle. Pay special attention to conditions far ahead of you.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need to use extra force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: You meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road width.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road width.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both vehicles need at least half of the road width to pass each other safely.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can get back to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
When your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You can only safely pass on a two-lane road when all three things are true: you can see clearly ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you, use your turn signal, and look for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: Which of these affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from too much drinking.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive carefully and reduce your speed. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog to light up the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you cannot see:
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Gets broken down by your body faster.
Reduces the number of driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions and makes you feel more confident. This leads to more driving errors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking, which could cause the car behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, visibility is poor. From half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever vehicles cannot be seen for 500 feet, drivers must use their headlights.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly and disrupting normal traffic flow is illegal. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.
